transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I feel constantly wound up and on edge, like I can’t relax even when I’m just at home with my family. It has gotten to the point where I just can't seem to shake this tension, and my wife urged me to finally come in and talk to someone.
Did these feelings start after a specific stressful event or major life change, or have they been going on for most days for at least 6 months without a clear trigger?

They've been happening almost every day for about nine months now. It started after a couple of major changes hit at once—my wife went back to work full-time after our second child was born, and I took on a high-visibility cloud migration project at my job.
Do you find yourself worrying about a lot of different things most days, and if so, is the worry hard to control even when you know it may be excessive?

Yes, I absolutely worry about so many different things every single day, from my kids and my parents' health to work deadlines and my marriage. It feels completely uncontrollable, like a constant chain of worst-case "what-if" scenarios that I just can't shut off, even when I try to tell myself to let things go.
When you feel this anxiety, do you also get physical symptoms like restlessness, muscle tension, fatigue, trouble concentrating, irritability, or sleep problems?

Yes, I have almost all of those. My shoulders are always tense and up by my ears, I'm constantly snapping at my wife, and I lie awake for hours only to wake up at 3 a.m. with my mind racing. It's gotten so bad that I can't even focus on my work meetings or code anymore without completely zoning out and going blank.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets criteria for generalized anxiety disorder: excessive anxiety and worry occurring nearly every day for about 9 months, involving multiple domains (family, health, work, marriage), difficulty controlling the worry, and associated symptoms including restlessness/feeling wound up, marked muscle tension, irritability, sleep disturbance, and impaired concentration. The symptoms are persistent and cause functional impairment at work and home.
